who: Historian of elections and modern Britain, University of Manitoba; PhD in Politics, Oxford, 1965.

evidence.says: Identifies Michael Kinnear as an assistant professor of history at Manitoba and author of The British Voter.
Page 145 reproduces an archival biography: Kinnear earned his Oxford doctorate in Politics in 1965 and joined Manitoba history that year; his works include The British Voter.
The indexed acknowledgements of John M. Cobb's 1991 dissertation identify Michael Kinnear as his advisor.
The other candidate, Michael S. Kinnear, is a discographer and researcher of the sound recording industry.

notes: Manitoba affiliation, Oxford doctorate, publication and named student agree. The discographer is a separate person.

who: Historian of antiquity and Greek philologist at Université du Québec à Montréal.

evidence.says: Her faculty profile lists Lussier's 2013 and Proulx's 2008 doctoral theses under supervised dissertations.
Identifies Auberger as a UQAM history professor with a doctorate in Greek philology and publications translating ancient historians.

notes: Both listed students are directly confirmed; institution and specialty match the authority record.

who: Labour and military historian at Wilfrid Laurier University, also known as John Terry Copp.

evidence.says: Laurier's archival biography identifies Copp as a labour and military historian and professor there from 1975 to 2017.
Identifies Terry Copp as a Laurier history professor and editor of Canadian Military History; records John Terry Copp as a name variant.
Laurier's repository names Terry Copp as Andrew Iarocci's thesis supervisor for his 2001 history MA.

notes: Authority and institutional career agree with the doctoral supervision period. Iarocci's MA confirms their earlier supervisory relationship; the two listed PhD theses were not independently located.

who: Historian of medicine and Quebec at Université Laval; author of La médecine au Québec.

evidence.says: Identifies the author of La médecine au Québec as a Laval history teacher with a master's in history from Laval.
The publisher identifies Bernier as the author of La médecine au Québec and a longstanding teacher of medical history in Laval's historical sciences department.
Stéphanie Tésio's contributor notice on printed page 285 says her Caen–Laval doctoral cotutelle was supervised by Daniel Teysseire and Jacques Bernier, specialists in medical history.

notes: Student supervision, institution, specialty and book identify n90709665 among the namesakes.

who: Anthropologist and science and technology studies scholar at MIT, subsequently UC Davis.

evidence.says: Records Dumit's MIT employment in connection with Cyborgs & Citadels and subsequently identifies him as a UC Davis anthropology professor.
Dumit's MIT homepage identifies him as an assistant professor of anthropology and science and technology studies in the STS program.
MIT's record of Nathan Greenslit's Pharmaceutical Relationships names Joseph Dumit as advisor and dates the HASTS PhD dissertation to 2007.
MIT's record of Anne Pollock's 2007 Medicating Race dissertation lists David S. Jones as advisor.

notes: Greenslit directly establishes the match. Pollock's repository advisor differs from the AHA attribution; this does not undermine Dumit's identity.

who: Anthropologist of Russia and the former Soviet Union at the University of Michigan, associated with Anthropology and History.

evidence.says: Identifies Lemon as a Michigan anthropology professor and director of its interdepartmental Anthropology and History program, researching Russia and the former Soviet Union.
The title page of Sonja Luehrmann's 2009 Forms and Methods dissertation names Alaina M. Lemon as doctoral committee chair.
The 2016 alumni list names Alaina Lemon as advisor of Weaving and Unraveling the Factory Town, listing its author as Luciana Nemtanu.

notes: Luehrmann's supervision is directly confirmed. The other dissertation matches by title and year, although Michigan lists the author under a different surname.

who: Professor of History and Political Science at the University of Victoria; PhD, European University Institute.

evidence.says: The faculty profile says Schmidtke joined UVic in 1999, lists his EUI doctorate and Politics of Identity, and names Constantin Chira (2005–2012) and Hanny Hilmy (2013–2015) as PhD students.
Identifies the author of Politics of Identity and Die Einhegung des Anderen as an associate professor and European studies scholar in political science at UVic.
The other Oliver Schmidtke authority is established for Architektur als professionalisierte Praxis.

notes: UVic affiliation, matching books and both students identify no97032389. Hilmy's faculty-page date range differs from the AHA year 2014.

who: Franklin Henry Giddings, professor of sociology and the history of civilization at Columbia University.

evidence.says: The authority cites The Elements of Sociology, whose title page identifies Franklin Henry Giddings as a Columbia sociology professor.
Columbia's finding aid lists Giddings's correspondence files for 1891–1928 and identifies him as professor of sociology and the history of civilization.
The alternative authority is for Frank D. Giddings, author of Strokes, published in 2003.

notes: Full name, Columbia appointment and period identify Franklin Henry Giddings. The individual student acknowledgements were not independently checked.
